Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The specific charge of the ions in beam A is greater than the specific charge of the ions in beam B

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the lower part of the figure is a velocity selector, with positive and negative plates; the ions enter the uniform magnetic field region inside the dashed box above from the same outlet above the velocity selector. In the magnetic field region there are “×” symbols drawn, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. After entering this same magnetic field, the ion beam separates into two curved trajectories A and B; judging from the degree of curvature shown in the figure, the trajectory of beam A bends more obviously, and its orbital radius is smaller than that of beam B. Then reason: The ions that can pass through the velocity selector satisfy the balance of electric field force and magnetic field force, so their velocities are the same, all being v=E/B. After entering the subsequent same uniform magnetic field, the charged particles undergo circular motion, and the orbital radius satisfies r=mv/(qB'), that is, r=v/(B'·q/m). Under the condition that v and B' are the same, the smaller the orbital radius r, the larger the specific charge q/m. Since the radius of beam A is smaller than the radius of beam B, the specific charge of the ions in beam A is greater than the specific charge of the ions in beam B.
